_about: Reviewed linguistic data (fil.nouns.relations): which studied nouns are collectives (no singular of their own; agreement as used), singulatives (the one of a collective) or one of a male/female pair, and the words their cards show beside them. `ar` is the indefinite nominative with full harakat; `lemma` is the corpus lemma|root when the Quran has the word. Every entry says why. Checked in every batch: `fil nouns batch plan` flags likely collectives.

إِبِل|أبل.why: اسم جمع: 'camels' as a herd, no singular of its own; one camel is جَمَل (male) or نَاقَة (female). Treated as feminine: الْإِبِلُ تَأْكُلُ, and its diminutive is أُبَيْلَة. No dual or plural of its own meaning (آبَال is rare, not Quranic). Triptote: إِبِلٌ إِبِلًا إِبِلٍ.

قَوْم|قوم.why: اسم جمع: a people, a group of men, no singular of its own. The Quran agrees with it both ways: قَالَ قَوْمُهُ (masculine) and كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ (feminine); pronouns referring to it are mostly masculine plural. Its plural أَقْوَام is not Quranic.

ناس|أنس.why: اسم جمع: people, no singular of its own; one person is إِنْسَان (same root). Treated as masculine plural: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ. The corpus tags it plural; it has no plural or dual of its own.

نَخْل|نخل.why: اسم جنس جمعي: date palms as a kind; one palm is نَخْلَة (Quran 19:23 جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ). Both agreements are Quranic: أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ (54:20) and أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ (69:7). نَخِيل is a separate lemma.

طَيْر|طير.why: اسم جنس جمعي (some count it a plural of طَائِر): birds; one bird is طَائِر (Quran 6:38 وَلَا طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ). Agreement in the Quran is feminine (وَالطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً 38:19, وَالطَّيْرُ صَافَّاتٍ 24:41) or masculine with the verb before it (غَرَّدَ الطَّيْرُ is correct).

تِين|تين.why: اسم جنس جمعي: figs; one fig is تِينَة (not in the Quran).

زَيْتُون|زيت.why: اسم جنس جمعي: olives, olive trees; one is زَيْتُونَة (Quran 24:35 شَجَرَةٍ مُبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ).

رُمّان|رمن.why: اسم جنس جمعي: pomegranates; one is رُمَّانَة (not in the Quran).

عِنَب|عنب.why: اسم جنس جمعي: grapes; one grape is عِنَبَة (not in the Quran). Its plural أَعْنَاب (vines, kinds of grapes) is Quranic and stays in the table.

شَجَرَة|شجر.why: اسم الوحدة: one tree, of the collective شَجَر 'trees' (Quran 55:6 وَالنَّجْمُ وَالشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ).

بَقَرَة|بقر.why: اسم الوحدة: one head of cattle, a cow, of the collective بَقَر (Quran 2:70 إِنَّ الْبَقَرَ تَشَابَهَ عَلَيْنَا). The bull is ثَوْر (not in the Quran).

عَبْد|عبد.why: The female of عَبْد (male slave, servant) is أَمَة (Quran 2:221 وَلَأَمَةٌ مُؤْمِنَةٌ). عَبْد of God is said of men and women alike.

كَلْب|كلب.why: The female of كَلْب (dog) is كَلْبَة (standard Arabic, not in the Quran).

مُؤْمِن|أمن.why: Reviewed: its feminine مُؤْمِنَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

كافِر|كفر.why: Reviewed: its feminine كَافِرَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

ظالِم|ظلم.why: Reviewed: its feminine ظَالِمَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

خَيْر|خير.why: Reviewed: خِيَرَة/خَيْرَات are other words (choice; good things), not a singulative of خَيْر.

جَبَل|جبل.why: Reviewed: جِبِلَّة (a multitude, a created nature) is another word; جَبَل is an ordinary noun with the plural جِبَال.

جَنَّة|جنن.why: Reviewed: جِنّ (jinn) and جُنَّة (shield) share the root but are other words; جَنَّة is an ordinary noun with the plural جَنَّات.

رَحْمَة|رحم.why: Reviewed: رَحِم (womb, kinship) shares the root but is another word, not a collective of رَحْمَة.

مَثَل|مثل.why: Reviewed: مِثْل (like, the same as) is another word; مَثَل is an ordinary noun with the plural أَمْثَال.

هُدًى|هدي.why: Reviewed: هَدْي (the sacrificial animal) is another word; هُدًى is a verbal noun with no plural.

لَيْل|ليل.why: Reviewed: لَيْل is night as a time, agreeing as a masculine singular (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى 92:1), not a group of nights; لَيْلَة (one night, لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ 97:1) is a word of its own whose plural لَيَالٍ the corpus files under لَيْل.

أَصْحاب|صحب.why: Reviewed: أَصْحَاب is the broken plural of صَاحِب (Quran 18:34 فَقَالَ لِصَاحِبِهِ), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

صالِح|صلح.why: Reviewed: its feminine صَالِحَة is the regular feminine of a participle (taught with the adjectives); صَالِح the prophet is a proper name.

وَجْه|وجه.why: Reviewed: وِجْهَة (a direction, 2:148) is another word; وَجْه is an ordinary noun with the plural وُجُوه.

بَيِّنَة|بين.why: Reviewed: the feminine of the adjective بَيِّن used as a noun (a clear proof), with the plural بَيِّنَات; not a singulative of a collective.

آباء|أبو.why: Reviewed: آبَاء is the plural of أَب (Quran 12:8 إِنَّ أَبَانَا), which the corpus files as its own lemma; a plural with a singular is not a collective.

أُمَّة|أمم.why: Reviewed: أُمّ (mother) shares the root but is another word; أُمَّة is an ordinary noun with the plural أُمَم.

صالِحَة|صلح.why: Reviewed: the regular feminine of the participle صَالِح, used as a noun (a good deed, الصَّالِحَات); not a singulative of a collective.

صادِق|صدق.why: Reviewed: its feminine صَادِقَة is the regular feminine of a participle, not a different word; agreement is taught with the adjectives.

نِساء|نسو.why: اسم جمع: women, no singular of its own root; one woman is امْرَأَة (Quran 4:12 أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ). نِسْوَة (12:30) is a second Quranic form of the same collective. Agreement is feminine: فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِسَاءً (4:11), نِسَاؤُكُمْ حَرْثٌ لَكُمْ (2:223) with feminine plural pronouns. (The corpus files امْرَأَة as امْرَأَت|مرأ, whose letters the relation check cannot match, so no lemma link.)

سَيِّئَة|سوأ.why: Reviewed: the feminine of the adjective سَيِّئ used as a noun (a misdeed), with the plural سَيِّئَات; سُوء (evil) is another word.

سُوء|سوأ.why: Reviewed: سَيِّئَة (a misdeed) is another word; سُوء is a verbal noun with no plural.

عَدُوّ|عدو.why: Reviewed: عُدْوَان (aggression) and عَدْو (running) are other words; عَدُوّ has the plural أَعْدَاء (it may also stand for a group: فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي 26:77).

نِعْمَة|نعم.why: Reviewed: نَعَم/أَنْعَام (livestock) share the root but are other words; نِعْمَة has the plurals نِعَم and أَنْعُم.
